clue.text: Plenty of silver stocked by British store originally

indicators.note: something stocked by a shop sits inside it, so silver goes within the other letters
originally points to the opening letter of the word store

parts.note: its first letter gives S
AG is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A British shop keeps a big supply of silverware in stock.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, having bags of something means having lots of it, an abundance.

parts.note: feeling low means feeling blue, downcast
a chip is a short lofted golf shot onto the green

explanation.surface: A golfer plays a superb low shot near the green.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue-chip shares are those of the most reliable companies, so the term means top-quality.

parts.note: ghastly means grim, horrible
Aldi is a discount supermarket chain

explanation.surface: A clown is seen inside a horrible supermarket.
explanation.walkthrough: Joseph Grimaldi was the celebrated Regency-era English clown, whose name is used for clowns generally.
explanation.definitionFit: Grimaldi was the famous early-nineteenth-century pantomime clown, so his name stands for a clown.

parts.note: plonker is British slang for a fool, an idiot
to embark on a ship or plane is to board it

explanation.surface: Someone urges a foolish person to get aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prompt' reads as a verb, but it is a noun: the device that prompts a presenter.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiot board is a cue card or screen held off-camera to prompt a television presenter with lines.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: moves suddenly and fast
second meaning: the game of throwing arrows at a board, a pub fixture

explanation.surface: A quick-moving game played in a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: To dart is to dash swiftly, and the game of throwing small arrows at a board is a pub classic.

clue.text: A regular at the Met, perhaps, in poorer age, unfortunately

definitions.text: A regular at the Met, perhaps

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters of poorer age are jumbled

explanation.surface: A Met regular struggles in a time of growing poverty.
explanation.walkthrough: The Met here is the Metropolitan Opera in New York, not the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who often attends the Metropolitan Opera House is a frequent spectator of opera performances.

parts.note: bright means cheerful, lively
a spark is a flash of light

explanation.surface: A clever person is described as cheerful and showy.
explanation.definitionFit: A bright spark is a clever, lively person, often said ironically.

parts.note: uniform means even, level

explanation.surface: An inspection of a US military outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uniform' looks like clothing; here it is the adjective meaning even. An A level is the British school-leaving exam taken at about eighteen.
explanation.definitionFit: A level is a British subject exam taken at the end of secondary school, used for university entry.

clue.text: Somewhere nice to live one leaving wants

indicators.note: one leaving means the numeral departs from the word for wants

parts.note: wants (noun) means desires
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A house-hunter's wish list for a pleasant place to live.
explanation.walkthrough: Des res is British estate-agent shorthand for a desirable residence.
explanation.definitionFit: Des res abbreviates desirable residence, the estate agents' phrase for an attractive home.

clue.text: Complete system may be inappropriate, if not loud

indicators.note: if not loud says to take the loud letter away from the word for inappropriate

parts.note: unfit means unsuitable, inappropriate
F is forte, the musical direction for loud

explanation.surface: A whole system might prove unsuitable unless kept quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a self-contained whole, an apparatus or assembly that works as one complete piece.

clue.text: Aberrant, sinner rose in a cantankerous state

indicators.note: aberrant means straying from the normal, so the letters of sinner rose are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wayward sinner gets up in a grumpy mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Orneriness is bad-tempered stubbornness, a grumpy and difficult disposition.

parts.note: CH is the chess abbreviation for check
a mo is a moment, a second
one's read as one is gives I (Roman one) plus S

explanation.surface: Someone checks a second item that is made of leather.
explanation.definitionFit: Chamois is soft pliable leather from goat or sheep skin, used for polishing cloths.

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters of role now less are mixed

explanation.surface: A great director's part has become less complicated.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is', linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Orson Welles directed Citizen Kane, among the most influential movies ever made.

clue.text: A grant secured by the hurdler, maybe

indicators.note: secured by means held within, so grant sits inside the word the

parts.note: to grant is to allow, let

explanation.surface: A sports grant has been won by the hurdler.
explanation.definitionFit: A hurdler is one example of a track-and-field sportsperson, hence the 'maybe'.

clue.text: Hardworking threesome on river with us

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after the river

parts.note: the Indus is a major river of Pakistan
a trio is a group of three

explanation.surface: Three diligent people by a river are joined by us.
explanation.definitionFit: Industrious means diligent, always busy at work.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Evelyn Waugh's novel is Brideshead ...
second meaning: gone back to see or study something once more

explanation.walkthrough: One meaning completes the title of Evelyn Waugh's novel; the other is the plain verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Waugh's 1945 novel is titled Brideshead Revisited, and to revisit something is to return to it.

definitions.meaning: second meaning: in British slang to sub someone is to lend them money ahead of payday

explanation.walkthrough: 'Forward' and 'subbed' look like football terms, but sub is British slang for an advance of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Advanced means far forward in progress, and money advanced is a loan paid early, a sub.

clue.text: Tie with father, full of energy and passion

indicators.note: full of means containing, so energy goes inside father

parts.note: dad is father
E is the physics symbol for energy
heat means intense passion

explanation.surface: A tie for a father who is energetic and passionate.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead heat is a race finishing level, with competitors tied.

clue.text: Serenade Ivy, hopelessly? Don't give up, no matter what

definitions.text: Don't give up, no matter what

indicators.note: hopelessly suggests a hopeless muddle, so the letters of Serenade Ivy are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lover keeps singing to Ivy despite no hope of success.
explanation.definitionFit: Never say die is an idiom urging persistence, refusing to quit.

clue.text: Conservative rebels in times of intense difficulty

parts.note: rises is a verb meaning rebels, as in rises up

explanation.surface: Tory MPs revolt during troubled times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rebels' reads as a noun, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Crises are emergencies, moments of acute trouble.

clue.text: A shiny paint — English celebrity put on litres

indicators.note: in a down clue, put on means placed above the litres

parts.note: a name is a famous person, a big name

explanation.surface: A famous English person applied litres of glossy paint.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamel paint dries to a hard glossy finish.

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
Angers is a city in western France

explanation.surface: A sports club operates in a French city.
explanation.walkthrough: Rangers is the Glasgow football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Rangers is a famous Scottish football team based in Glasgow.

clue.text: A week facing custody may be difficult to deal with

indicators.note: facing means set against or next to, so the week comes before custody

parts.note: to be in ward is to be in custody or guardianship

explanation.surface: A week spent in custody could be hard to handle.
explanation.definitionFit: An awkward person or situation is hard to manage or tricky.

parts.note: recent means new

explanation.surface: A decent, newly arrived American deputy leader.
explanation.walkthrough: Spiro Agnew was Richard Nixon's vice-president.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiro Agnew served under Nixon before resigning in 1973.

clue.text: Easy to name leader of several nitwits

parts.note: easy means simple

indicators.note: leader of points to the opening letter of the word several

parts.note: its first letter gives S

explanation.surface: It's easy to identify which of several fools is in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Simpletons are foolish people, idiots lacking sense.

indicators.note: nursing means holding close, so husband goes inside the word for one

parts.note: an ace is the one in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A woman is caring for her husband, who is in pain.
explanation.definitionFit: An ache is a dull continuous pain.

parts.note: not a tiny amount, as the idiom suggests, but a literal drop of something into the sea

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom means a negligible amount; read literally, it is a spacecraft dropping into the sea at the end of a mission.
explanation.definitionFit: A splashdown is a space capsule landing on the sea under parachutes.

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Rewrite a portion of a document set in italics.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit text is to revise or rephrase it.
